_note: Reviewed wording per language, applied to every translation (MASTERSPEC 7.6). 'rules' are added to the translation prompt; a translation containing a 'forbidden' word (any case) is rejected and retried like an invented number; 'fixed' strings replace the model's wording for that key. 'all' applies to every language. Add a language's entries when its review sheet comes back; mark it reviewed in contracts/copy/labels.json.

rules: "Multiplex" means a building with several homes. Never translate it as a word for a set number of homes, such as duplex or triplex.
A City of Toronto ward is a "quartier" ("Quartier 04", "dans ce quartier"). Never use "circonscription", which means a riding.
A house lot is a "terrain" ("terrains résidentiels", "ce terrain"). Never use "lot" or "lots".
"Residential house zones" are "zones résidentielles" (R, RD, RS, RT, RM). Never call them "unifamiliales": they allow multiplexes.

fixed.heading_blocking_rule: Pourquoi les terrains ne conviennent pas

rules: "Too close to call" is "trop serré pour trancher", as in the briefing.
"Doesn't fit" is "ne convient pas". Never "ne rentre pas".
An attached house is a semi or row house: "une maison jumelée ou en rangée". A detached house is "une maison individuelle". Never "attachée" or "détachée".
"This is a screening, not a permit" is always "Il s'agit d'une vérification préliminaire, et non d'un permis." Never "dépistage".
"The City's zoning examiner" is "l'examinateur du zonage de la Ville". Never leave the English word "zoning".
"Short by 0.15 m" is "il manque 0,15 m". Never "ce qui manque de".
